'''Peter Wadhams''' ScD (born 14 May 1948) is emeritus<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/research|title=Research &#124; Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics}}</ref> professor of Ocean [[Physics]], and Head of the Polar Ocean Physics Group
in the [[Faculty of Mathematics, University of Cambridge|Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics]], [[University of Cambridge]]. He is best known for his work on [[sea ice]].

==Career==
Wadhams has been the leader of 40 polar field expeditions.<ref name="damtpppw">{{cite web |url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/people/p.wadhams/ |title=Professor Peter Wadhams |work=Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics |publisher=[[Centre for Mathematical Sciences (Cambridge)]] |accessdate=10 August 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171208155922/http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/people/p.wadhams/ |archive-date=8 December 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Wadhams advocates for the use of [[climate engineering]] to [[mitigation of climate change|mitigate climate change]].<ref name="gmb">{{cite journal |url=http://www.scientificamerican.com/article/geoengineering-last-chance-save-sea-ice/ |title=Geoengineering May Be Our Best Chance to Save Sea Ice |date=13 November 2012 |journal=Scientific American |publisher=Nature America  |doi=10.1038/scientificamerican1212-12 |accessdate=10 August 2015 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Attempting to estimate when the [[Arctic Ocean]] will be "[[Arctic sea ice decline|ice-free]]", Wadhams in 2014 predicted that by 2020 "summer sea ice to disappear,"<ref>{{cite news |author1=Craig Medred |title=Expert predicts ice-free Arctic by 2020 as UN releases climate report |url=https://www.adn.com/arctic/article/expert-predicts-ice-free-arctic-2020-same-day-un-releases-climate-report/2014/11/02/ |access-date=9 January 2021 |work=[[Anchorage Daily News]] |date=2 November 2014 |quote="By 2020, one would expect the summer sea ice to disappear. By summer, we mean September. ... (but) not many years after, the neighboring months would also become ice-free."  Wadhams later clarified that by "ice-free" he did not exactly mean the Arctic was going to look like the Baltic Sea in summer.}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author1=Sarah Knapton |title=Experts said Arctic sea ice would melt entirely by September 2016 - they were wrong |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/science/2016/10/07/experts-said-arctic-sea-ice-would-melt-entirely-by-september-201/ |access-date=9 January 2021 |work=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |date=8 October 2016 |quote=Prof Wadhams, a leading expert on Arctic sea ice loss, has recently published a book entitled A Farewell To Ice in which he repeats the assertion that the polar region would free of ice in the middle of this decade.}}.</ref>  Wadhams and several others have noted that [[climate model]] predictions have been overly conservative regarding [[sea ice]] decline.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Overland |first1=J. E. |last2=Wang |first2=M. |s2cid=129474241 |doi=10.1002/grl.50316 | title = When will the summer Arctic be nearly sea ice free? |journal = Geophysical Research Letters |volume=40 |issue=10 |pages = 2097 | year = 2013 |bibcode = 2013GeoRL..40.2097O |doi-access= }}</ref>

In 2021, Wadhams was the Chairman of Science Committee for [[Extreme E]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.extreme-e.com/en/science-team|title = Extreme e - the Electric Odyssey}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
*1977 [[W. S. Bruce Medal]] for his oceanographic investigations, especially in studying the behaviour of pack ice near Spitsbergen, the North Pole and off east Greenland<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.geos.ed.ac.uk/~rsgs/awardsandmedals/wsbruce.pdf |title=Archived copy |accessdate=2016-10-20 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20161020114617/http://www.geos.ed.ac.uk/~rsgs/awardsandmedals/wsbruce.pdf |archivedate=2016-10-20 }}</ref>
*1987 [[Polar Medal]]
*1990 Italgas Prize for Environmental Sciences
